docs.title: Server Slow Troubleshooting Flow
docs.text:
```mermaid flowchart TD A([Alert: Server Slow]) --> B{Can you SSH?} B -->|No| C[Check VM, network, firewall, console] B -->|Yes| D[Check uptime and load average]

D --> E{Load average high?}
E -->|Yes| F[Check CPU with top, ps, pidstat]
E -->|No| G[Check memory with free and vmstat]

F --> H{High CPU process found?}
H -->|Yes| I[Identify process owner and application]
H -->|No| J[Check IO wait and kernel activity]

G --> K{Swap used or memory low?}
K -->|Yes| L[Check OOM logs and top memory processes]
K -->|No| M[Check filesystem]

M --> N{Filesystem full?}
N -->|Yes| O[Clean logs, check deleted files, extend LVM]
N -->|No| P[Check disk IO with iostat]

P --> Q{IO wait high?}
Q -->|Yes| R[Investigate storage or VMware datastore]
Q -->|No| S[Check network and application logs]

S --> T([Document RCA and verification])

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Runaway process
  • Java garbage collection
  • Backup or batch job
  • Database query
  • Monitoring or security scan

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
• Confirm owner of process
  • Restart or stop approved process
  • Tune application or schedule
  • Escalate if process is business-critical

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• No space left on device
  • Application cannot write logs
  • Login or service startup failure

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
df -h
df -i
du -xh /var | sort -h | tail -20
find /var/log -type f -size +100M -ls
lsof | grep deleted

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
• Compress or remove approved old logs
  • Clean temporary files
  • Restart process holding deleted files if approved
  • Extend LVM/filesystem if required

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text: Check whether memory is used by application RSS, filesystem cache, shared memory, or swap pressure.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Memory should stabilise and swap activity should reduce.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Application process killed unexpectedly
  • Server becomes slow or unresponsive
  • dmesg shows OOM messages
  • Swap usage increases rapidly

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
free -h
swapon --show
vmstat 1 10
ps aux --sort=-rss | head -20
dmesg -T | grep -i -E 'oom|killed process'
journalctl -k | grep -i oom

docs.title: Possible Causes
docs.text:
• Application memory leak
  • Java heap too large
  • Batch job consumed memory
  • Not enough RAM for workload
  • Swap misconfiguration

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
• Restart leaking process after approval
  • Tune application heap or memory limit
  • Add memory if recurring
  • Review cron or batch schedule

docs.title: Verification

free -h
vmstat 1 10
dmesg -T | grep -i oom

docs.title: Key Point
docs.text: High load is not always high CPU. It can also be blocked IO, disk latency, NFS hang, or many runnable processes.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
uptime
vmstat 1 10
top
iostat -xz 1 5
ps -eo state,pid,ppid,cmd | awk '$1 ~ /D|R/ {print}'

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text:
• R state usually points to CPU pressure
  • D state usually points to IO wait or blocked storage

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• SSH login is slow
  • Application response time is poor
  • Monitoring alert for CPU, memory, IO, or load
  • Users report timeout or degraded performance

docs.title: First Checks
docs.text:
uptime
hostnamectl
df -h
free -h
vmstat 1 10
top

docs.title: Decision Flow
docs.text:
Server slow
├── High CPU?       top, mpstat, pidstat
├── High memory?    free, vmstat, ps --sort=-rss
├── High IO wait?   iostat, iotop, sar -d
├── Disk full?      df -h, df -i, du
├── Network issue?  ss, ping, traceroute, sar -n
└── App issue?      logs, systemctl, journalctl

docs.title: Resolution Examples
docs.text:
• Restart problematic service after approval
  • Clear safe temporary files or old logs
  • Stop runaway batch job
  • Escalate to application/database/network/storage team
